claim_verdicts.description: Mapper interface with signature mapEntry(key: K1, values: Values<V1>, context: Context): Iterable<[K2, V2]>
claim_verdicts.quote: export interface Mapper<K1 extends Json, V1 extends Json, K2 extends Json, V2 extends Json> { mapEntry(key: K1, values: Values<V1>, context: Context): Iterable<[K2, V2]>; }

claim_verdicts.description: Reducer interface with initial, add(accum, value), remove(accum, value) returning A | null
claim_verdicts.quote: export interface Reducer<V extends Json, A extends Json> { initial: A | null; add(accum: A | null, value: V & DepSafe): A; remove(accum: A, value: V & DepSafe): A | null; }

claim_verdicts.description: Reducer.remove() must satisfy correctness constraint: remove/add idempotence
claim_verdicts.quote: If `remove` returns a non-`null` value, then it **must** be equal to calling `add` on each of the values associated to the key, starting from `initial`. That is, `accum`, `add(remove(accum, value), value)`, and `remove(add(accum, value), value)` must all be equal for any `accum` and `value`

claim_verdicts.description: Entry<K, V> type defined as [K, V[]]
claim_verdicts.quote: export type Entry<K extends Json, V extends Json> = [K, V[]];

claim_verdicts.description: LazyCollection interface with getArray(key: K): V[] and getUnique(key: K) methods
claim_verdicts.quote: export interface LazyCollection<K extends Json, V extends Json> extends AbstractLazyCollection, Managed { getArray(key: K): (V & DepSafe)[]; getUnique(...): V & DepSafe; }

claim_verdicts.description: RFC 008 quote: 'A reactive service defines a compute graph made of skip runtime reactive collections'
claim_verdicts.quote: A *reactive service* defines a compute graph made of skip runtime reactive collections, along with one or more *reactive resources* (analogous to REST resources), which are parameterized, dynamically generated, read-only, skip runtime reactive collections exposed to the outside world.

claim_verdicts.description: sum.ts example contains Plus mapper implementing Mapper<string, number, string, number>
claim_verdicts.quote: class Plus implements Mapper<string, number, string, number> { mapEntry(key: string, values: Values<number>): Iterable<[string, number]> { return [[key, values.toArray().reduce((p, c) => p + c, 0)]]; } }

adequacy_assessment.readme_purpose: Skip's core incremental engine: the language/runtime split, reactive collections, mappers/reducers, and a concrete comparison of what this buys over ordinary database reactivity.

coverage.language_runtime_split: comprehensive - Section 1 explains compiler (Skip language) vs runtime (skipruntime-ts) separation with directory structure
coverage.reactive_collections: comprehensive - Section 2 covers EagerCollection, LazyCollection, multi-map representation, dependency tracking, entry-level granularity updates
coverage.mappers_reducers: comprehensive - Sections 1-2 explain Mapper and Reducer interfaces, the add/remove contract, memoization, incremental deltas with concrete examples
coverage.database_comparison: comprehensive - Section 4 provides concrete example (tweet counting by user) showing O(1) Skip incremental vs O(n) database full re-scan, explains operator-level delta propagation, memoization, graph optimization, watermarks, reducer correctness guarantees
